Please fix Signed-off-by.
Done, Thanks.
Can we avoid creating unstructured logs now for future platforms (Yv5, SB, etc.)?

Yes, but there doesn't seem to be a suitable log-create message id to use for these GPIO messages at the moment, such as this active Button Event commit.
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/80259
So I think maybe that's the only way to do it for now...

Except for the button type GPIOs, the rest of the GPIOs are used to alert the motherboard PCIE CLK issue.

Our hardware team think these logs to be important, can We keep these logs?
Done

Can we get elaboration from the hardware team on what the events are to be used for?  Usually events and errors are for DC-side diagnostics and requirements come from the RTP side.  I'm not very excited about trying to log every GPIO and/or create custom events that aren't standardized.  Non-standard events don't show up in Redfish push events anyhow, so they're not particularly useful.

Can't the sequence of button presses, etc. be pulled from the systemd journal for debugging purpose?

We have removed all non-standardized SEL records.
And we are continuing to confirm with the hardware team whether logging these GPIOs is necessary. 

If logging is required, we will attempt to use standardized SEL records or change to journal logging in the future.
Why do we have so many GPIOs we need to configured to "default values"?  Shouldn't those be configured in hardware to appropriate defaults?
After discussing with the hardware team, we only keep the necessary parts.
Is this potentially changing system state?  What if the BMC reboots while the server is powered on?
After discussing with the hardware team, we only keep the necessary parts.
"reserved"?  Why are we needing to adjust a reserved GPIO?
After discussing with the hardware team, we only keep the necessary parts.
What does this mean?  Why the raw i2cset?

At POC stage, we temporarily notify BIOS that the BMC is ready through CPLD.
At EVT, we will use SGPIO instead, but this part is still under going.
